items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: the brass band was played, John, and they had a trumpet player, who was Dutry, used to play in the brass band

ctx.x: at the Lincoln Park. Yeah. Yeah, the, the band was stopped. The brass band? No, no, and they had, John had his, his orchestra too. Yeah. On a big stage, yeah. Playing from fourth, to seventh, seven, they'd knock off for lunch, then they'd go, in a big hall, they'd go to their halls, and play from eighth to fourth.

Well, let me tell you about that. You see, I used to go out, go out to that park, I was a kid, in short pants, and, uh, the brass band was played, John, and they had a trumpet player, who was Dutry, used to play in the brass band, alongside, with another trumpet player, from Al Jays, I've been trying to think of his name, real dark. Buddy Johnson. No, not Buddy, it wasn't Buddy. Harrison Bourne? Him, Harrison Bourne. He used to play, he used to play, in John's brass band, see, but John was playing bass drum,…
